Got drunk, made out with a drunk girl that JUST threw up, mixed myself a nice Listerine and vodka cocktail, and then danced with a door. Or at least that's what my drunk-ass friends told me.

My buddies parents were gone for the weekend,so he was having a party. I was hammered. At some point it occurred to me that I was hungry. I went to the kitchen to look for food, but anything even remotely edible was already gone. But then, in the refrigerator, way in back on a bottom shelf I found two blueberry pancakes in plastic wrap. I was ecstatic. I ate the first one and it was cold and dry and terrible, but I didn't care, I was so hungry.

I was about to eat the second when I had a brilliant idea. I would wrap it back up and hide it so I would have something to eat later. Drunkenly congratulating myself on my foresight, I went back to paryting, and passed out on the floor a couple hours later.

I woke up in a few hours feeling like shit, and starving. After trying to figure out how I was going to get something to eat, I had hazy recollection of stashing that second blueberry pancake. "Yay! Good job drunken self! " I thought, and started making my way through the debris and passed-out bodies toward the kitchen.

I opened the refrigerator, worried that someone else had found my blueberry pancake, but there it was! I pulled it out, unwrapped it and realized that those weren't blueberries. It was covered in mold.

My parents were out of town for the week of 4th of July. So highschool tux thought it would be an amazing idea to have a rager. I took everything breakable, locked it away, threw tarps down on the floors etc. Totally wanted to protect the house.

Once we started drinking, the two beer pong tables outside weren't enough, so we turned the tables inside into pong as well. Some people were in the pool, others were casually setting off fireworks in the backyard. You know, typical 4th party. Everyone is hammered.

Girl I had a crush on, we'll call her "Jen", grabs my wrist and says 'I need to tell you something'. She leads me to my bedroom, and I find "Rachel" (previous FWB, Jen's bff) sitting on my bed. Turns out both of them had been wanting to have a threesome, and figured this was a good night.

Mid act, we hear a massive boom followed by intermittent pops. Concerned we stop, and I run downstairs. "John" had lit a mortar on the porch, but had dropped it and let it roll into the living room. Other people were playing beer bong with firecrackers, and trowing lit bottle rockets into the pool. I do my best to stop the craziness, but the party was on a role. I spent the rest of the night essentially protecting the house from my drunk friends.

A core group of people stayed the night (Jen, Rachel and John included), and spent the whole next day cleaning up. We ended up repainting a section of the living room from where the mortar left burn marks. We also had to fish all of the bottle rocket parts out of the pool. When all was said and done, the house looked exactly the same again. I was shocked, and thought I was actually going to get away with it. Nope, the minute my parents got home, my neighbor walked over and told them the whole story. My mom was furious, and my dad was impressed.

TLDR: Had drunken 4th of July party, threesome interrupted by fireworks, cleaned house and was ratted out by neighbors. Over all 11/10 would do again.

Jonathan Rauch's book, Government's End, does a good job explaining how this is. As an example, we often see a big economic boom during the peacetime in affected countries following wars because the slate is essentially cleared: there are no interest groups (e.g. lobbying, corrupt government political groups) holding the country back, so everything can run with few things gumming up the works. As you would imagine, this is not a desirable situation for interest groups and their counterparts, corporations, since they in particular get wiped out. These same interest groups are the reason that we have so much useless legislation and questionable subsidies and tax breaks.

And as an aside, the basic concept behind these groups is that it's a lot more profitable to make a play for a greater slice of the pie for your smaller group (e.g. $10,000 divided by 10 companies), than it is to work towards increasing EVERYONE'S production by $5 worth.
